scenes.visual: Title card 'New Neighbours' over a hollow ball of cells. Reuses the first film's COLOUR MAP (both films): egg cytoplasm pale cream; inherited material (determinant) PURPLE dots; signals between cells GREEN arrows; ectoderm BLUE, mesoderm RED, endoderm YELLOW; calcium wave bright white-cyan. All numbers appear only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: A ball of cells has to become a body with an outside, a middle and a gut. How do surface cells get inside, and does it matter whom they meet?
scenes.visual: A hollow ball of cream cells (cut away to show its fluid cavity), label 'blastula'. Beside it a simple tadpole outline with three nested tubes: outside, middle, gut, all grey for now. Question mark between them.
scenes.narration: A ball of cells has to become a body with an outside, a middle and a gut. How do surface cells get inside, and does it matter whom they meet?

scenes.tts: The first film showed cleavage cutting the egg into cells, each with its own slice. Purple marked what a cell inherits. Cleavage makes new contacts as cells divide, but it does not rearrange the whole embryo.
scenes.visual: Brief replay from the first film: 32-cell embryo inside its fixed outline, PURPLE cells outlined. Furrows pinch and each division adds contacts between sister cells; label 'cleavage partitions the egg'. A second label waits beside it: 'gastrulation: large-scale movement inside and germ-layer rearrangement'.
scenes.narration: The first film showed cleavage cutting the egg into cells, each with its own slice. Purple marked what a cell inherits. Cleavage makes new contacts as cells divide, but it does not rearrange the whole embryo.

scenes.tts: Gastrulation is the stage that does. Cells travel from the surface to the inside, and sort into three germ layers. Ectoderm, in blue, stays outside. Mesoderm, in red, forms the middle. Endoderm, in yellow, lines the inside.
scenes.visual: Cells on the ball's surface flow inward. The embryo resolves into three nested layers, coloured as named: BLUE ectoderm outer, RED mesoderm middle, YELLOW endoderm innermost, each labelled as it appears. Caption 'gastrulation'.
scenes.narration: Gastrulation is the stage that does. Cells travel from the surface to the inside, and sort into three germ layers. Ectoderm, in blue, stays outside. Mesoderm, in red, forms the middle. Endoderm, in yellow, lines the inside.

scenes.tts: Embryos get cells inside by several movements. In invagination, a sheet bends inward, like a finger pushed into a soft ball.
scenes.visual: Side-on cartoon of a sheet of cells: one region dents inward into a pocket; a ghost finger pressing a soft ball appears in an inset. Label 'invagination (sea urchin gut begins this way)'.
scenes.narration: Embryos get cells inside by several movements. In invagination, a sheet bends inward, like a finger pushed into a soft ball.

scenes.tts: In involution, a sheet rolls over an edge and spreads along the inside. In a frog, cells roll in over the lip of the blastopore, the opening where they enter.
scenes.visual: Side-on cartoon: a sheet rolls over a lip and runs back underneath itself, arrows showing the roll. A frog embryo inset with a crescent-shaped opening labelled 'blastopore' and its edge labelled 'lip'.
scenes.narration: In involution, a sheet rolls over an edge and spreads along the inside. In a frog, cells roll in over the lip of the blastopore, the opening where they enter.

scenes.tts: In ingression, single cells leave the sheet and move inward, one at a time. Embryos combine these movements to bring cells inside.
scenes.visual: Side-on cartoon: individual cells detach from a sheet and crawl inward. Then all three cartoons shrink side by side and merge into one embryo where a bend, a roll and single cells each carry a different group of cells inward, building the BLUE-RED-YELLOW layers together; caption 'embryos combine movements'.
scenes.narration: In ingression, single cells leave the sheet and move inward, one at a time. Embryos combine these movements to bring cells inside.

scenes.tts: Moving inside does something else. Cells now sit next to cells they never touched before. Can a neighbour change what a cell becomes?
scenes.visual: Zoom into the layers: a RED cell that has moved inside now touches a BLUE cell above it, a contact line flashing. A faint GREEN arrow with a question mark points from one to the other.
scenes.narration: Moving inside does something else. Cells now sit next to cells they never touched before. Can a neighbour change what a cell becomes?

scenes.tts: Hilde Mangold tested this with newt embryos. She cut out a piece of the dorsal lip of the blastopore, the edge on the future back side.
scenes.visual: Caption 'Hilde Mangold, newt embryos (published with Hans Spemann, 1924)'. A pale newt embryo with its blastopore; the dorsal lip glows and a small piece is lifted out with a fine tool. Label 'dorsal lip'.
scenes.narration: Hilde Mangold tested this with newt embryos. She cut out a piece of the dorsal lip of the blastopore, the edge on the future back side.

scenes.tts: The donor came from a pale newt species. She grafted the piece onto the belly side of a darker embryo, from a related species. The host grew a second body axis.
scenes.visual: The pale piece is placed on the belly (ventral) side of a darker host embryo, labels 'pale donor species' and 'dark host species'. The host develops into a larva with its normal axis plus a second partial body axis on its belly side, outlined (schematic).
scenes.narration: The donor came from a pale newt species. She grafted the piece onto the belly side of a darker embryo, from a related species. The host grew a second body axis.

scenes.tts: If the graft built that second axis only from its own inherited material, what colour would the new axis be?
scenes.visual: Close-up of the second axis in silhouette, colour hidden. Two swatches: 'pale (graft)' and 'dark (host)'. Question card.
scenes.narration: If the graft built that second axis only from its own inherited material, what colour would the new axis be?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds; 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: It was not all pale. Dark host cells were part of it. The graft had recruited them. It told host cells what to become.
scenes.visual: The second axis fills in: pale graft cells mixed with dark host cells (schematic proportions). GREEN arrows spread from the pale graft into the surrounding dark host cells, which then join the axis.
scenes.narration: It was not all pale. Dark host cells were part of it. The graft had recruited them. It told host cells what to become.

scenes.tts: Remember the crescent: colour showed where it went, not what it did. Here colour still only traced cells. The graft was the test, and colour showed host cells joined in.
scenes.visual: Split screen: left, the first film's purple crescent with 'where it goes'; right, the pale-and-dark second axis with two labels: 'graft = the test' and 'colour = who built what'. A tick appears on the right.
scenes.narration: Remember the crescent: colour showed where it went, not what it did. Here colour still only traced cells. The graft was the test, and colour showed host cells joined in.

scenes.tts: A signal from one group of cells that changes the fate of its neighbours is called induction. The grafted tissue is called the organizer.
scenes.visual: GREEN arrows from the graft to neighbouring cells; label 'induction'. The pale graft gets a label 'organizer'.
scenes.narration: A signal from one group of cells that changes the fate of its neighbours is called induction. The grafted tissue is called the organizer.

scenes.tts: So a cell's fate has two sources. Purple: what it inherits from its slice of egg. Green: what its new neighbours tell it. Most embryos studied closely use both.
scenes.visual: One cell in centre. PURPLE dots inside it labelled 'inherits'; GREEN arrows arriving from its neighbours labelled 'is told'. Caption 'most embryos studied closely use both'.
scenes.narration: So a cell's fate has two sources. Purple: what it inherits from its slice of egg. Green: what its new neighbours tell it. Most embryos studied closely use both.

scenes.visual: End card (Hex card) with one line only: 'Fate follows from what a cell inherits and what it is told.'
